historical_anchor: Historical USS Harder sank Minazuki 6 Jun, Hayanami 7 Jun and Tanikaze 9 Jun around Tawi Tawi; this cluster is not auto-inherited because branch Tokai/MAD/patrol/escort integration is materially better.

branch_centerline.result: Harder closes the oiler/escort traffic but is localized earlier by the layered patrol picture and cannot reproduce the historical Minazuki kill. Minazuki survives; escorts and aircraft expend time/depth charges.

Harder shifts outside the strongest patrol box and still obtains one high-quality attack opportunity. Hayanami is sunk. This preserves the ability of an exceptional US submarine to break the screen despite branch ASW improvement.
Route changes, denser search and rapid warning dissemination reduce repeated attack geometry. The historical Tanikaze kill is not inherited; Tanikaze survives the window.

The mobile fleet remains under real submarine pressure: training windows are shortened/rotated and escort fuel/sonar/depth-charge expenditure rises, but the historical three-destroyer catastrophe is reduced to one destroyer loss.

ASW_interpretation: Improvement reduces repeated exposure and increases datum-to-escort handoff; it does not make US submarines harmless or prevent a skilled boat from scoring.
guard: Do not apply the historical Minazuki and Tanikaze June losses later unless a new branch event creates them.
